description: Introduces 2025 budget adjustments, proposing a 5.2% property tax.
Details investments in police, transit, and roads.

chips.text: Councillor Davies noted this budget was the best start in 12 years, reducing it before kickoff.
Saskatoon's population grew by 46,000 residents since 2018, projected to 2025.

description: Preliminary 2025 budget discussions will start at a 5.2% tax increase.

chips.text: Received as information
11 for, 0 against
Administration proposed starting 2025 budget discussions at 5.2%, down from 5.84%.

description: Saskatoon Public Library levy increases 2.8% for 2025.
Police Service adds 24 new frontline officers.
City's major venues and services continue operations.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Mayor Block emphasized housing vulnerable people improves community safety.
Police will create a dedicated warrant enforcement team.
Provincial funding for 24 police officers is a once-in-a-generation opportunity.
Residents expressed strong concerns about crime and safety.
Police flagged a pending binding arbitration award for wages.
Remai Modern offers low-sensory events for children with autism.
Remai Modern developing its first environmental plan.
Police will hold a special meeting for wage recommendation by December 18.

segments.title: TCU Place budget and operations
segments.takeaway: Tammy Sweeney presented TCU Place's 2024 projected financials and 2025 budget, highlighting industry changes, increased costs, and a projected deficit to be covered by reserves.

segments.title: SAS Health Center budget and operations
segments.takeaway: John Howden and Todd Gray Choski presented SAS Health Center's successful 2024 events and 2025 budget, including capital items like new chairs and parking lot repairs.

segments.title: Remai Modern budget and operations
segments.takeaway: Eileen Burns and Aing London presented Remai Modern's fourth consecutive break-even financial result, highlighting increased visitors, community partnerships, and a reconciliation plan.

segments.title: Saskatoon Public Library budget and operations
segments.takeaway: Carol Shepstone presented the SPL's 2025 budget, requesting a 2.8% levy increase, and discussed the new central library project and community engagement.

segments.title: Saskatoon Police Service budget and operations
segments.takeaway: Commissioner Grace and Chief McBride presented the SPS's revised 2025 budget, requesting additional funding for 24 frontline officers due to increased call volumes and provincial support.

description: Committee recommends renewing Nutrien Wonderhub lease with phased-in cost increases.
Wonderhub faces $400,000 deficit; seeks rent relief.
City provides $250,000 annual in-kind rent contribution.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Fork noted some Wonderhub exhibits are in disarray and staff engagement is low.
Nutrien Wonderhub, a children's museum, faces a $400,000 deficit for 2024-25.
Nutrien Wonderhub requested Option 4, including rent relief and no new building charges.
Wonderhub cited ambiguous lease wording, potentially contravening new building repair charges.
Wonderhub is implementing a government relations strategy to secure provincial operating grants.

segments.title: Administration presents lease renewal options
segments.takeaway: Administration outlines financial considerations for Nutrien Wonderhub's lease renewal, recommending option two to phase in facility cost increases over five years.

segments.title: Questions for administration on lease details
segments.takeaway: Councillors question administration on market value rent, total city contributions to Wonderhub, and the museum's operating budget.

segments.title: Nutrien Wonderhub CEO presents case for Option 4
segments.takeaway: The CEO requests Council approve a decision aligned with option 4, seeking rent relief or additional grant funding and opposing new charges for building repairs and insurance.

segments.title: Questions for Wonderhub CEO on operations and funding
segments.takeaway: Councillors inquire about admission fees, provincial funding efforts, fundraising, exhibit maintenance, operating hours, and the overholding provision.

segments.title: Motion to approve administration's recommendation
segments.takeaway: Councillor Donnelly moves to approve the administration's recommendation, which is seconded by Councillor Dubois.

segments.title: Discussion on proposed amendment and recess
segments.takeaway: Councillor McDonald proposes an amendment to remove additional costs while maintaining base rent increases, leading to a recess for drafting.

description: Recommends 4.96% property tax increase for 2025.
Adds $500,000 to snow budget, funds fire inspectors.
Approves WonderHub operating costs for five years.

chips.text: Recommended
That the 2025 Operating Plan approved by City Council on November 28, 2023
Councillor Parker raised concerns about underfunding asset management plans.
Councillor Donnar preferred a lower snow budget increase than approved.
Legal dispute exists over WonderHub lease costs and interpretation.
Fire bylaw inspectors support unhoused individuals and community safety.
Councillor Davies committed to more transit safety staff next year if needed.

segments.title: Initial Presentation and Process
segments.takeaway: The CFO presented the 2025 Business Plan and Budget proposed adjustments, outlining initial recommendations and the process for council deliberations.

segments.title: Franchise Fee Revenue Reduction Motion
segments.takeaway: Councillor Dubois moved to eliminate the proposed $500,000 reduction to franchise fee revenue, which was seconded and added to the consideration list.

segments.title: Parking Revenue Reduction Motion
segments.takeaway: Councillor Dubois moved to eliminate the proposed $500,000 reduction to parking revenues, which was seconded and added to the consideration list.

segments.title: Accessible Parking Permit Fee Discussion
segments.takeaway: Council discussed the recent increase in accessible parking permit fees and the financial impact of leaving it at $60, but no motion was made.

segments.title: Transit Safety and Community Support Officers
segments.takeaway: Council received an update on the Community Support Officers program on transit, discussing its effectiveness and future reporting on safety outcomes.

segments.title: Snow Service Levels and Budget Discussion
segments.takeaway: Council discussed current snow service levels and budget risks, leading to motions for a jurisdictional scan and additional funding for snow events.

segments.title: CVCM and SLNP ROI Reduction Motions
segments.takeaway: Council introduced motions to eliminate additional contributions to the Civic Building Comprehensive Maintenance reserve and the Saskatoon Light & Power return on investment phase-in reduction.

segments.title: Initial Voting on Consideration List Items (Day 1)
segments.takeaway: Council voted to add several items to the consideration list for final budget approval, including a snow and ice jurisdictional scan and various financial adjustments.

segments.title: Snow and Ice Budget Final Vote (Day 2)
segments.takeaway: After extensive discussion and multiple amendments, council approved adding $500,000 to the snow and ice budget for a sixth snow event.

segments.title: Franchise Fee Revenue Final Vote
segments.takeaway: Council voted to eliminate the proposed $500,000 reduction to franchise fee revenue, maintaining the original forecast.

segments.title: Parking Revenue Final Vote
segments.takeaway: Council voted to eliminate the proposed $500,000 reduction to parking revenues, maintaining the original forecast.

segments.title: 2025 Budget Final Approval
segments.takeaway: Council unanimously approved the 2025 civic budget, resulting in a 4.96% property tax increase for the municipal portion.
